ai.title: Add agent-template.d.ts type definitions for custom agents
ai.summary: New `common/src/templates/agent-template.d.ts` provides TypeScript definitions for building custom Codebuff agents. Exports `AgentConfig` and `AdvancedAgentConfig` interfaces, plus union types for `ToolName`, `ModelName`, and `SpawnableAgentName`. Includes ready-to-use examples like `FileEditorExample` and `AdvancedExample` to demonstrate configuration patterns.

eli5.text: If you build your own helper inside the Codebuff toolkit, the system now hands you a ready-made checklist of allowed settings, so filling in your helper's personality, model, and capabilities feels more like picking from labeled boxes and less like guessing. The toolkit will warn you the moment you type an unsupported tool name, model, or agent to spawn, preventing silent mistakes before they run. You don't need to change anything in your existing helpers to keep working; the new definitions are purely additive safety rails for authors writing brand-new helpers today.

ai.title: Use xdg-open for Linux browser launch in CLI
ai.summary: Updated login browser launch logic in `npm-app/src/client.ts` to use `xdg-open` on Linux platforms, replacing the generic `open` command. Previously, the code defaulted to `open` for all non-Windows systems, which failed on Linux environments lacking that specific binary. This change ensures correct cross-platform behavior by selecting `start` for Windows, `xdg-open` for Linux, and `open` for macOS.

eli5.text: When you log in to the tool from a Linux computer, a separate browser window now opens to complete sign-in where it previously might not have opened at all. The software now detects it is running on Linux and uses the standard Linux command (xdg-open) to launch your web browser, instead of trying a macOS command that doesn't exist on Linux. No steps from you are required; the browser should just open the login page automatically when you run the login command on a Linux machine.

ai.title: Improve agent-template.d.ts type strictness and docs
ai.summary: Refined `ModelName` and `SpawnableAgentName` types in `common/src/templates/agent-template.d.ts` to use `(string & {})` instead of `string` for custom values. Added a reference link to OpenRouter models in the `ModelName` documentation. This preserves autocomplete for known models while allowing arbitrary strings.

eli5.text: If you configure an agent with a model that isn't in the built-in list, your custom model name will now only need to be a plain text string instead of something that looks like a specific keyword. This affects anyone who sets up custom AI agents, and you would notice that custom names still show helpful suggestions for common models while you type, rather than being treated as a completely free-form entry.

ai.title: Deprecate assistantMessage and assistantPrefix in agent templates
ai.summary: Removed assistantMessage and assistantPrefix fields from AgentOptions and agent templates. File-picker agent now uses handleSteps generator instead of initialAssistantMessage for tool calls. runProgrammaticStep syncs state.messages to agentState.messageHistory and injects tool call strings as user messages. Affects backend/src/run-agent-step.ts, run-programmatic-step.ts, and all agent template files.

eli5.text: When you ask a file-picking helper to find something in your code, it no longer relies on a pre-written opening message that used to trigger its tool calls. Instead, it now generates each action step-by-step from scratch, and the system feeds the results back in as if you had typed them. If you looked, you'd see fewer canned phrases at the start of its replies and more direct, on-demand tool usage. This is live today for anyone using agent-powered features.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.441
ai.summary: Updated package version from 1.0.440 to 1.0.441. This change applies to `npm-app/release/package.json`.

eli5.text: If you use the AI coding assistant, you may notice it can now open your web browser correctly on Linux computers during the login process. The version label of the software you install was bumped from one release to the next, and this particular release includes a small update ensuring Linux users get redirected to their default browser when they sign in, rather than encountering a broken or unsupported launch step. You would only notice this if you're on Linux and you tried to log in; it's a behind-the-scenes fix that makes an existing feature actually work for you.

ai.title: Fix spawn-agents logger parentId reference
ai.summary: Corrects logger.debug parentId reference in backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agents.ts to read from subAgentState. Fixes type safety by explicitly annotating subAgentState as AgentState. Scope limited to internal agent spawning handler. Ensures accurate debug logging for spawned agent hierarchies.

eli5.text: When the system quietly spawns helper agents to work behind the scenes, debug logs now correctly record which parent agent each helper came from. Previously, those logs pointed to an outdated reference, so tracking agent families was unreliable; this fixes that. It's housekeeping that improves logging accuracy for internal troubleshooting only.

ai.title: Consolidate agent config types and refine system prompt
ai.summary: Merges `AdvancedAgentConfig` into `AgentConfig`, making `systemPrompt` optional and adding `userInputPrompt` for per-turn instructions. Updates `handleSteps` to use strict `Generator` types with defined `AgentState` and `ToolResult` instead of `any`, and changes default version to `0.0.1`. Scope limited to `common/src/templates/agent-template.d.ts`. Examples updated to demonstrate `userInputPrompt` usage and type alignment.

eli5.text: You can now give this assistant a set of step-by-step instructions that it follows every time you ask it to do something new, instead of only one big background instruction that never changes. The developers also cleaned up the configuration so all the settings live in one place, the version numbering is clearer, and they added a real example showing how to use the new instructions. This is in place today and ready to use.
